newsitem.title: CHINA: China parliament chief rules out superpower status.
newsitem.headline: China parliament chief rules out superpower status.

text.p: A Chinese leader on Wednesday moved to reassure the world over China's growing economic and military might, saying it would never become a superpower and would always be a force for peace.
Poor or rich, China would not threaten other nations, the Xinhua news agency quoted Qiao Shi, head of the National People's Congress, or parliament, as saying.
"China will never become a superpower and will always be a force safeguarding peace in Asia and in other parts of the world," Qiao said.

"Historically, China was invaded and bullied repeatedly by foreign powers, but we will not be a threat to others whether we are very poor and are experiencing great difficulties or doing better economically," Xinhua quoted him as saying.
The three million-strong People's Liberation Army is the biggest in the world, and China's military build-up in recent years has caused anxiety among neighbours.
Beijing, which has clashed repeatedly with neighbours along its long land and sea borders, says its programme of military modernisation is purely defensive.
China ruffled regional feathers in March 1996 when it conducted missile tests and war games near Taiwan in the run-up to the island's first direct presidential elections.
"In the future, when China has become developed and when its overall national strength has increased, it will make further contributions to world peace and stability," Xinhua quoted Qiao as saying.
"To develop, China needs a long-term stable, peaceful international environment, and it is of particular importance for China to maintain good relations with its neighbours," he said.
